balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom. From FY2025 the company also discloses an operating profit under Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS) that, unlike the Hong-Kong-standard OperatingIncome charted here, folds in associate income and finance costs -- the DCF treats the two bases separately rather than splicing one series onto the other.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • HKFRS vs CAS operating profit diverging once both bases have a few periods of history

profitSplit.title: Profit before NCI vs net income to parent
profitSplit.content:
Profit for the period incl. NCI is consolidated profit before splitting it between the parent's shareholders and minority shareholders; net income here is what is left for Huadian Power's own H-share/A-share holders after that split.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: many of its plants are only 50-85% owned (Hubei 82.56%, Jiangsu Huadian Energy 80%, Laizhou 75%, Weifang 64.29%), so a meaningful slice of group profit never reaches parent shareholders. The FY2025 acquisition of 80% of Jiangsu Huadian Energy and seven other entities widened this gap further.

What to watch:

  • The NCI share of profit widening after an acquisition, diluting the earnings growth parent shareholders actually see
  • Years where incl.-NCI profit and net income move in different directions (one subsidiary swinging the consolidated number while parent profit holds steady, or vice versa)

nciPerpetual.title: Non-controlling interests and perpetual capital securities
nciPerpetual.content:
Non-controlling interests (NCI) is the minority shareholders' claim on the equity of partly-owned subsidiaries. Perpetual capital securities are a hybrid instrument with no maturity date -- accounted for as equity because Huadian Power has no obligation to repay principal, but carrying their own distributions (see Interest Paid chart's sibling, Perpetual Distributions Paid, below), which makes them economically closer to debt than to ordinary equity.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: NCI roughly doubled from ~RMB19.3bn (FY2024) to ~RMB32.9bn (FY2025) on the Jiangsu Huadian Energy deal, and perpetual securities have run RMB20-32bn across recent half-years -- together these hybrid and minority claims are now a similar order of magnitude to the whole of parent shareholders' equity. A reader who prices this stock off reported "equity" without separating the two is valuing capital that is not entirely the H-share/A-share holders' to claim. Perpetual distributions paid (not separately charted -- disclosed only in annual filings, ~RMB0.4-1.1bn/yr) are deducted ahead of ordinary dividends.

What to watch:

  • NCI and perpetual balances growing faster than shareholders' equity
  • New perpetual issuance used to fund growth without diluting the share count, at the cost of a senior-to-equity distribution claim

interestPaid.title: Interest paid
interestPaid.content:
Interest paid is cash interest on borrowings, shown annually only (the company does not break this out at half-year).

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: with ~RMB101-133bn of total debt, mostly floating-rate, this line tracks PRC interest-rate policy more than company-specific credit risk -- and it sits alongside, not instead of, the perpetual distributions paid to perpetual-security holders above.

What to watch:

  • Interest paid rising faster than total debt (rate risk, not just leverage)
  • Coverage of interest paid by operating cash flow

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Huadian Power International Corporation Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
